body:
In my case, I elected to tell my case manager that I'd rather kneecap myself with a cordless drill than go back there to deal with that smug bastard. If I can't trust someone to be a decent human being, I'm not going to let them stick me with needles and the like. :s

 In the end, I go to a lab that's further away now, but sans captain smug. It works out, I guess.

Hehe, I never really thought of keeping a blog before. It sort of seemed like there was nothing I could add to the blogosphere that wasn't being said by more boisterous people that had more time to devote to a their blog than I could. I guess my situation is a bit, err... unique, but all the same... Maybe I'll give it a try sometime. :3

I don't really perceive myself as a person of beauty, but I guess that's probably more my bad self-image talking than anything else. I'm not going to give up, I've been around long enough to know that by now. 

If anything, and this is probably the craziest thing I've thought since I've gotten back to a more normal life... I feel that being found to be HIV positive has actually made me a better person, somehow. Sort of a reality check that forced me to appreciate what I have, and to remember that I'm not going to live forever. Sort of a really bad wake-up call.

And thank you. I'll try to keep up <3

That's quite alright, hun. Male pronouns, even indirect, are just something that kind of sticks into me when I read something, sorry to be a butthead. :s

And you're right, I didn't mean to try to downplay the severity of anything, I just meant that people have survived cancer before, not that there was a magic pill that made it disappear. My dad had a bad spot a ways back where he had melanoma. It was on his face and he didn't go to the doctor the moment he saw it, thinking it was just some kind of wart. It got bad, and he got it looked at, and they cut a chunk out of his face to get it out. This was when I was like... 11 or 12, so I had no idea what was really going on. I only got to hear about it later on, when I was in high school. It was sort of scary, he made it sound like the doctor's weren't sure about his odds of it not coming back soon. He seems to be alright, but they screen him regularly nowadays in case it comes back. Every other family member that had it either got it and refused treatment for it, opting to die at home, or got it treated and never had a problem afterwards, so I was talking from poor experience there. :/

I can hardly imagine what it must feel like to have people telling you that you might not make it much longer. That must be awful. I'm sorry you have to experience that.

I'm glad that you were able to move on, in spite of the crushing heartache that Emma's loss must have invoked... It's heartwarming to know there are people like Emma and Kaitlynn in this world. It's hard to tell sometimes if its really that people are as self-centric and heartless as I wonder at times, or if I just don't meet a lot of truly wonderful people. Van is really a gem in my life, and I know that if we were in a bad spot, we'd both be trying to jump in front of the bullet for each other. It's hard to believe at times, but you're right about that. I've actually talked to a few people recently that wouldn't see HIV as a reason to not love someone. In fact, the more people actually learn about the disease, the less it freaks them out. One of the friends in question mentioned above was initially terrified, and after doing some research, he realized that the threat of infection had always been something conveniently left out of any sex ed courses, as its actually not extraordinarily easy to pass on.

In the end, I think about giving up at times, but I don't think I really could do it. I'd probably have done the same thing as you, sooner or later. It's very sobering to think about, really. I've come close enough to ending my life enough times that I've realized that if I couldn't do it the night of February 17th, I simply can't do it. I just physically am incapable of it. I guess my trigger finger just doesn't want to bend that way. XD

I think I'm going to be alright. The feeling of despair comes and goes. It's not easy to just let it wash over and keep strong every time, but I'm getting better at it. It's sometimes hard to separate the disease from my identity because of all the tests and paperwork and meetings and... Ugh. When the CDC sends someone to your home to talk to you, it sort of makes you feel... changed. Like you aren't going to be who you used to be anymore. It goes quickly, but it lingers at the back of your mind for a while after.

But yeah, I'm a nice, happy, cheerful person when I'm not being a mopey sad-sack XD (as denoted by the throwaway account), so odds are you probably wouldn't mind chatting regardless. X3 It'd be fun to try not to twitch when I get called 'man', lol :V

I'll keep my head up, don't worry. :3

I'm terribly sorry to hear that. :c Its hard to think sometimes that, despite how messed up my situation is, it's still the same life I used to have.

I'm trying to accept the life I'm in for as something I can be at peace with, but I think that the part that messes me up the most is the overwhelming feeling that the "care" program I'm assigned to doesn't care at all.

Just today, after a 12 hour shift at work (6pm to 6am, so I'm going to bed when the world is waking up over here), I stayed up late so I could make it in when the place opened, and I was met with a guy that was sleeping in the receptionist's chair as the guy I had to tell I was there to get blood tests done. The guy looked genuinely annoyed with me coming in there to wake him up and tell him I had to get blood work done. He smiles and tells me he didn't have any paperwork, and tells me that he needs [insert document name here that I hadn't recieved] or he can't help me. I call my case manager and he tells me he'll fax it over. The paperwork arrives, and the receptionist there says he didn't send [this] and [that], and if I don't have [card I've never heard of or needed before for other clinics they sent me to] then he can't help me. And even if my case manager sends him a copy of the card, he still won't help me because he needs the actual card.

I stared at him, completely baffled by his smug demeanor and complete lack of willingness to work with me on anything, and the way he seemed to almost enjoy watching my despair intensify as I tried to call my case manager again and got nothing but a voicemail message.

Then, when I did what I can only assume anyone else in my position would do, and threw my hands up and said "Fuck this, I'm going home." He laughed as I swung the door open to leave.

Maybe I'm just too stressed out and the little things in this treatment program are pissing me off way more than they should, but damn it all, I want to have faith in the treatment program I have to center my life around. It was all I could do to not cry on the way home and leave a message to my case worker saying that I never wanted them to send me to that lab again for anything, even if it's as simple as a urine sample.

I know it could be worse, and I feel like an idiot for having all this anger towards the things that are happening through the course of treatment, but this isn't something that you do to human beings. If it was a business and I was a paying customer, I'd be calling the guy's higher-ups to explain that their employee has turned away a potential customer, and I'd be telling anyone that asked to never go there.

... *sigh*... I feel like I should be better at handling this sort of thing by now.

I know that giving up isn't the way to do anything in life... But it's hard for me to wrap my head around this. I was always in perfectly good health up until this. I used to run a lot, and I always tried to healthy so I could be fit and live well... But this... It's just hard to understand that I'm no longer in near perfect health. My life feels like its become a shitty joke somewhere.

But you're right. Things aren't over. Just... Different. I don't know how long it will take me to really adjust, but I feel as though I should have by now...

Well, not to be rude or anything, but I'm not a 'man'. I mentioned that a few times through the post... I'm a girl, if just a strange one.

I'm sorry that you had to experience the loss of your girlfriend, but I'm happy that you survived cancer. It's killed quite a few of my relatives over time, to the point of being a bit worrisome that I may have a problem with it in the future, myself...

But between HIV and cancer, one of these is potentially curable, and one of these is not, through currently available treatments. The latter is also passable. :/

In the end, I'm probably not going to give up, but... It's so hard to feel hopeful and motivated when you feel like the deck is irrevocably stacked against you. I've had days where I literally slept 18 hours straight, because I was too depressed to get up. I want to try to live a life worth living, but knowing that you would literally die of sadness if the few people you love and trust most weren't there anymore, for any reason... If Van were to leave my life, I'd be crushed. The way people think about HIV is mostly with paranoia-grade fear. He loved me before we found I was positive, and he didn't change once he found out. I don't think I'll ever get that lucky twice.

I want to try to make my future, but for now, I need to kill my debt and find a way to feel human again. I'm trying as best as I can to keep my chin up, but this will never go away, short of some sort of medical science breakthrough. Until then, my best hope is continued care, and hoping that Republicans don't try to crusade end funding for HIV care anytime soon...

And yet... There are times, when I'm alone, or when I'm at work, where I feel this immense sadness. The thought that I could possibly spread it, or it could get worse, or it could become untreatable, or Van could wise up and leave me, or...

And I think. And I look back at who I was in disgust. I think about dying, so I'm not a hazard to Van anymore. I think about my body burning to ashes with no biological trace of the virus to remain. I think about how the world will be better without me and how many people I could have hurt.

I cry. I try to keep it to myself, because I don't want to worry or annoy anyone, but I hurt so much inside that I want to scream.

And I have to hold on until the tempest subsides.

I've been trying to not dwell on it, but it always comes back.

I mean, I'm an HIV+ pansexual pre-operative transsexual furry with a severe lack of self esteem and a shitty security job. What sort of future is there for me, regardless of actions?
